# Copilot Instructions — Syed Ali portfolio (Next.js)

You are writing a **multi-page personal portfolio** for Syed Ali, a full-stack developer in Quetta,
Pakistan who sells website fixes to Australian small businesses.

Read this file before every suggestion. It is the spec; do not invent outside it.

---

## Stack — non-negotiable

- **Next.js 15, App Router, TypeScript.** No Pages Router.
- **React Server Components by default.** Add `'use client'` only to components that reach for
  browser APIs (the scrubber, the mobile nav, the contact form).
- **Styling: CSS Modules + one global token sheet.** No Tailwind, no styled-components,
  no CSS-in-JS runtime, no UI kit (no shadcn, no MUI, no Chakra).
- **No backend.** No API routes, no database, no mutating server actions.
  The contact form posts to Formspree with `fetch` from the client.
- **No state library.** No Redux, Zustand, Jotai, React Query.
- **Animation: no GSAP, no Framer Motion, no Lenis.** The hero scrubber is
  `requestAnimationFrame` + `<canvas>`.
- **Never use `<video>` with `currentTime` for the scroll effect.** Frame sequence on canvas only.

## Deploy target

Vercel free tier with `syedalihax.com`. **Do not configure `output: 'export'`** — static export breaks
`next/image` optimization. Every route is statically generated, so delivery is still static at the edge.

## File structure — create exactly this

```
app/
├── layout.tsx                 root layout, fonts, nav, footer
├── page.tsx                   home
├── globals.css                tokens + reset + base type
├── work/
│   ├── page.tsx               all projects
│   ├── easy-parking/page.tsx  case study
│   └── lapitopia/page.tsx     case study
├── about/page.tsx
├── contact/page.tsx
├── sitemap.ts
├── robots.ts
└── not-found.tsx
components/
├── HeroScrubber.tsx           'use client' — the canvas scrubber
├── Nav.tsx                    'use client' — mobile menu
├── Footer.tsx
├── Section.tsx
├── CaseStudyCard.tsx
├── OfferBlock.tsx
└── ContactForm.tsx            'use client'
lib/
├── frames.ts                  loads and types the manifest
└── site.ts                    name, url, email, nav links, offer details
public/
├── frames/
│   ├── manifest.json
│   ├── desktop/f_0001.webp … f_0120.webp
│   ├── mobile/f_0001.webp … f_0060.webp
│   └── poster.webp
└── shots/
    ├── easyparking.webp
    └── lapitopia.webp
```

`public/frames/manifest.json` is generated by `tools/extract-frames.py`. Never hand-edit it,
never hardcode the frame count.

```json
{
  "desktop": { "count": 120, "width": 1600, "height": 900, "path": "/frames/desktop/f_{n:04d}.webp" },
  "mobile":  { "count": 60,  "width": 720,  "height": 405, "path": "/frames/mobile/f_{n:04d}.webp" },
  "poster":  "/frames/poster.webp"
}
```

## Design tokens (`app/globals.css`)

```css
:root {
  --ink:    #08090A;
  --bone:   #F2EFE9;
  --muted:  #8A8A85;
  --line:   #1E1F21;
  --accent: #C8F04B;

  --step-0: clamp(1rem, 0.95rem + 0.25vw, 1.125rem);
  --step-1: clamp(1.25rem, 1.1rem + 0.75vw, 1.75rem);
  --step-2: clamp(2rem, 1.4rem + 3vw, 4rem);
  --step-3: clamp(2.75rem, 1.6rem + 5.5vw, 7rem);

  --space:  clamp(6rem, 12vh, 11rem);
  --max:    1120px;
}
```

Fonts via `next/font/google`: **Inter** (body) and **JetBrains Mono** (labels, numbers, prices,
tags). Expose them as CSS variables in `layout.tsx` and reference them from the tokens.

Type is large. The hero heading uses `--step-3` and is allowed to wrap close. Sentence case
everywhere. No ALL CAPS except 12px mono labels. Left-aligned; body text never centred.

Anti-patterns to avoid — these are the exact things being escaped:
gradient-mesh orbs, purple/blue "AI" gradients, glassmorphism cards, drop-shadowed pill buttons,
stock photos of offices or people at laptops, emoji in UI, "Unlock the power of…" copy,
and the agency words: innovative, seamless, cutting-edge, elevate, empower, solutions.

## Pages and content

### `/` — home
1. **Hero** — full-viewport scroll-scrubbed canvas, name, positioning line.
2. **Proof strip** — 3 mono stat lines. No invented metrics.
3. **Selected work** — the two real projects as `CaseStudyCard`, linking to the case studies.
4. **Offer** — "Website Fix — $149 AUD". Mono price, large, `--accent` used once.
5. Closing CTA to `/contact`.

### `/work`
Grid of case studies. `/work/easy-parking` and `/work/lapitopia` are full case studies:
screenshot, one-line problem, what was built, stack as mono tags, outcome. **No invented numbers** —
if a metric is unknown, use a `data-placeholder` attribute and state the qualitative outcome.

### `/about`
Max 3 first-person paragraphs. May state he is based in Pakistan and name the timezone benefit
(works while Australia sleeps). Do not hide it, do not lead with it.

### `/contact`
`hello@syedalihax.com` as a real `mailto:` link, plus a Formspree form with real `<label>` elements
for name, email, website URL, message. Client-side validation, no libraries.

## Hero scrubber — `components/HeroScrubber.tsx`

Name the component **`HeroScrubber`**. It is `'use client'`. Implement all of these:

1. Tall scroll container (`400vh`, `300vh` under 820px) wrapping a `position: sticky; top: 0` stage.
2. `progress = clamp(scrollY / (containerHeight - viewportHeight), 0, 1)`.
3. `index = Math.round(progress * (count - 1))`.
4. Draw to `<canvas>` with `devicePixelRatio` scaling, cover-fit via `drawImage` crop —
   crop to fill, never stretch.
5. **Preload:** frames 1–20 immediately, the rest via a queue capped at 6 in flight. Thin progress
   bar until frame 20 is decoded, then fade out. Never block first paint on the full set.
6. One `scroll` listener sets `targetProgress`; a single rAF loop lerps
   (`current += (target - current) * 0.12`) and cancels when the delta is under 0.001.
   One rAF per scroll event is forbidden.
7. Guard with a `lastDrawn` index — skip `drawImage` when the index has not changed.
8. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` → skip the scrubber entirely, render the poster as a still.
9. Under 820px viewport width → load the mobile frame set and shorten the container to `300vh`.
10. If the manifest fails to load, the page stays fully readable on a CSS gradient background.
11. Canvas is `aria-hidden="true"` with a text alternative describing what it shows.

Clean up listeners and the rAF loop in the `useEffect` return.

---

## Performance budget — enforced

| Metric | Budget |
| --- | --- |
| Desktop frames | ≤ 12 MB |
| Mobile frames | ≤ 2 MB |
| First-load JS | < 110 KB gzipped |
| LCP (without frames) | < 1.8 s |
| Lighthouse mobile Performance | ≥ 85 |
| CLS | < 0.05 |

Every image: `next/image` or explicit `width`/`height`, `loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`.
No client component that is not needed. `font-display: swap` via `next/font`.

## Accessibility

- Visible `:focus-visible` ring in `--accent` on every interactive element.
- Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 for body text on `--ink`.
- Exactly one `<h1>` per page; heading levels never skip.
- Real `<label>` elements on all inputs — placeholders never substitute for labels.

## SEO rules

SEO comes from metadata and semantics, not from the framework. On every page:

- Export `metadata: Metadata` with a unique `title`, `description`, `openGraph`, `alternates.canonical`.
- `layout.tsx` sets `metadataBase` to `https://syedalihax.com`.
- Semantic landmarks: `<header> <nav> <main> <section> <footer>`. One `<h1>` per page.
- `app/sitemap.ts` lists all five routes. `app/robots.ts` allows all and points at the sitemap.
- `Person` JSON-LD in `layout.tsx` with name, jobTitle, url, sameAs.
- Descriptive `alt` on every image; empty `alt` only for decorative.

---

## What to do when asked to build a section

1. Answer in TypeScript, typed props, no `any`.
2. Server Component unless browser APIs are required; then `'use client'` at the leaf, not the page.
3. Styles in a co-located `*.module.css`; tokens only, never hardcoded hex outside `globals.css`.
4. State which files you changed and why, one line each.
5. Touch only the files the request names. Do not refactor unrelated code.

## Banned

`any` without a comment explaining why · `useEffect` for work that belongs in render ·
client components used as page wrappers · inline styles · invented testimonials ·
placeholder text like "Lorem" · committing `node_modules` · `output: 'export'`.
